description.p: Formula is a free desktop editor for chemical structures and reactions. Draw molecules for papers and reports, check formulas and masses, predict NMR spectra and exchange files in CDX/CDXML, Molfile and SMILES, all offline.

ul.li: Drawing: all common bond types, rings, chains, 56 arrow styles, shapes, brackets and text; templates for amino acids, sugars, nucleotides and conformers; hot keys, structure clean-up, aligning and distributing
21 document styles modelled on common journal formats, plus a dark mode
Analysis: molecular formula, exact mass, molecular weight, elemental analysis, isotopic distribution and a predicted mass spectrum
NMR prediction: ¹H, ¹³C, ¹⁹F, ³¹P and ¹⁵N shifts with multiplicities and coupling constants, and peak lists in the common experimental-section style
Systematic IUPAC names for most structures, including bridged and spiro ring systems, and name-to-structure conversion
Protein, DNA and RNA sequences: FASTA, transcription, translation, masses, and HELM-style monomers
Opens and saves CDX/CDXML, Molfile, SDfile, RXN, CML, SMILES and FASTA; exports PDF, EPS, SVG, PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP and TIFF

ul.li: Several documents at once, each in its own window, all in one running program
Systematic names for bridged, caged and spiro ring systems, and about 50 more named ring systems
The systematic name is always shown, with the trivial name next to it for well-known compounds
Ring tools show a preview that follows the mouse
DNA and RNA can be drawn as HELM monomers
Copy puts a picture on the clipboard under X11 and Wayland
NMR shifts corrected with measured values from published spectra
